content:
Chapter: V1 - Encoding and Sanitization
Section: V1.1 - Encoding and Sanitization Architecture
Requirement ID: V1.1.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that input is decoded or unescaped into a canonical form only once, it is only decoded when encoded data in that form is expected, and that this is done before processing the input further, for example it is not performed after input validation or sanitization.
summary: Verify that input is decoded or unescaped into a canonical form only once, it is only decoded when encoded data in that form is expected, and that this is done before processing the input further, for example it is not performed after input validation or sanitization.

content:
Chapter: V1 - Encoding and Sanitization
Section: V1.1 - Encoding and Sanitization Architecture
Requirement ID: V1.1.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the application performs output encoding and escaping either as a final step before being used by the interpreter for which it is intended or by the interpreter itself.
summary: Verify that the application performs output encoding and escaping either as a final step before being used by the interpreter for which it is intended or by the interpreter itself.

content:
Chapter: V1 - Encoding and Sanitization
Section: V1.2 - Injection Prevention
Requirement ID: V1.2.1
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required, such as encoding the relevant characters for HTML elements, HTML attributes, HTML comments, CSS, or HTTP header fields, to avoid changing the message or document structure.
summary: Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required, such as encoding the relevant characters for HTML elements, HTML attributes, HTML comments, CSS, or HTTP header fields, to avoid changing the message or document structure.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V1.2.1: Injection Prevention

content:
Chapter: V1 - Encoding and Sanitization
Section: V1.2 - Injection Prevention
Requirement ID: V1.2.10
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that the application is protected against CSV and Formula Injection. The application must follow the escaping rules defined in RFC 4180 sections 2.6 and 2.7 when exporting CSV content. Additionally, when exporting to CSV or other spreadsheet formats (such as XLS, XLSX, or ODF), special characters (including '=', '+', '-', '@', '\t' (tab), and '\0' (null character)) must be escaped with a single quote if they appear as the first character in a field value.
summary: Verify that the application is protected against CSV and Formula Injection. The application must follow the escaping rules defined in RFC 4180 sections 2.6 and 2.7 when exporting CSV content. Additionally, when exporting to CSV or other spreadsheet formats (such as XLS, XLSX, or ODF), special characters (including '=', '+', '-', '@', '\t' (tab), and '\0' (null character)) must be escaped with a single quote if they appear as the first character in a field value.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V1.2.10: Injection Prevention

content:
Chapter: V1 - Encoding and Sanitization
Section: V1.2 - Injection Prevention
Requirement ID: V1.2.2
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that when dynamically building URLs, untrusted data is encoded according to its context (e.g., URL encoding or base64url encoding for query or path parameters). Ensure that only safe URL protocols are permitted (e.g., disallow javascript: or data:).
summary: Verify that when dynamically building URLs, untrusted data is encoded according to its context (e.g., URL encoding or base64url encoding for query or path parameters). Ensure that only safe URL protocols are permitted (e.g., disallow javascript: or data:).

Section: V1.5 - Safe Deserialization

Verification Level: L2

Verify that deserialization of untrusted data enforces safe input handling, such as using an allowlist of object types or restricting client-defined object types, to prevent deserialization attacks. summary: Verify that deserialization of untrusted data enforces safe input handling, such as using an allowlist of object types or restricting client-defined object types, to prevent deserialization attacks. summary: Verify that different parsers used in the application for the same data type (e.g., JSON parsers, XML parsers, URL parsers), perform parsing in a consistent way and use the same character encoding mechanism to avoid issues such as JSON Interoperability vulnerabilities or different URI or file parsing behavior being exploited in Remote File Inclusion (RFI) or Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.1 - Generic OAuth and OIDC Security
Requirement ID: V10.1.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that tokens are only sent to components that strictly need them. For example, when using a backend-for-frontend pattern for browser-based JavaScript applications, access and refresh tokens shall only be accessible for the backend.
summary: Verify that tokens are only sent to components that strictly need them. For example, when using a backend-for-frontend pattern for browser-based JavaScript applications, access and refresh tokens shall only be accessible for the backend.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.1.1: Generic OAuth and OIDC Security

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.1 - Generic OAuth and OIDC Security
Requirement ID: V10.1.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the client only accepts values from the authorization server (such as the authorization code or ID Token) if these values result from an authorization flow that was initiated by the same user agent session and transaction. This requires that client-generated secrets, such as the proof key for code exchange (PKCE) 'code_verifier', 'state' or OIDC 'nonce', are not guessable, are specific to the transaction, and are securely bound to both the client and the user agent session in which the transaction was started.
summary: Verify that the client only accepts values from the authorization server (such as the authorization code or ID Token) if these values result from an authorization flow that was initiated by the same user agent session and transaction. This requires that client-generated secrets, such as the proof key for code exchange (PKCE) 'code_verifier', 'state' or OIDC 'nonce', are not guessable, are specific to the transaction, and are securely bound to both the client and the user agent session in which the transaction was started.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.1.2: Generic OAuth and OIDC Security

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.2 - OAuth Client
Requirement ID: V10.2.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that, if the code flow is used, the OAuth client has protection against browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF), which trigger token requests, either by using proof key for code exchange (PKCE) functionality or checking the 'state' parameter that was sent in the authorization request.
summary: Verify that, if the code flow is used, the OAuth client has protection against browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF), which trigger token requests, either by using proof key for code exchange (PKCE) functionality or checking the 'state' parameter that was sent in the authorization request.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.2.1: OAuth Client

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.2 - OAuth Client
Requirement ID: V10.2.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that, if the OAuth client can interact with more than one authorization server, it has a defense against mix-up attacks. For example, it could require that the authorization server return the 'iss' parameter value and validate it in the authorization response and the token response.
summary: Verify that, if the OAuth client can interact with more than one authorization server, it has a defense against mix-up attacks. For example, it could require that the authorization server return the 'iss' parameter value and validate it in the authorization response and the token response.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.2.2: OAuth Client

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.2 - OAuth Client
Requirement ID: V10.2.3
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that the OAuth client only requests the required scopes (or other authorization parameters) in requests to the authorization server.
summary: Verify that the OAuth client only requests the required scopes (or other authorization parameters) in requests to the authorization server.

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.3 - OAuth Resource Server
Requirement ID: V10.3.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the resource server only accepts access tokens that are intended for use with that service (audience). The audience may be included in a structured access token (such as the 'aud' claim in JWT), or it can be checked using the token introspection endpoint.
summary: Verify that the resource server only accepts access tokens that are intended for use with that service (audience). The audience may be included in a structured access token (such as the 'aud' claim in JWT), or it can be checked using the token introspection endpoint.

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.3 - OAuth Resource Server
Requirement ID: V10.3.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the resource server enforces authorization decisions based on claims from the access token that define delegated authorization. If claims such as 'sub', 'scope', and 'authorization_details' are present, they must be part of the decision.
summary: Verify that the resource server enforces authorization decisions based on claims from the access token that define delegated authorization. If claims such as 'sub', 'scope', and 'authorization_details' are present, they must be part of the decision.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.3.2: OAuth Resource Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.3 - OAuth Resource Server
Requirement ID: V10.3.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that if an access control decision requires identifying a unique user from an access token (JWT or related token introspection response), the resource server identifies the user from claims that cannot be reassigned to other users. Typically, it means using a combination of 'iss' and 'sub' claims.
summary: Verify that if an access control decision requires identifying a unique user from an access token (JWT or related token introspection response), the resource server identifies the user from claims that cannot be reassigned to other users. Typically, it means using a combination of 'iss' and 'sub' claims.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.3.3: OAuth Resource Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.3 - OAuth Resource Server
Requirement ID: V10.3.4
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that, if the resource server requires specific authentication strength, methods, or recentness, it verifies that the presented access token satisfies these constraints. For example, if present, using the OIDC 'acr', 'amr' and 'auth_time' claims respectively.
summary: Verify that, if the resource server requires specific authentication strength, methods, or recentness, it verifies that the presented access token satisfies these constraints. For example, if present, using the OIDC 'acr', 'amr' and 'auth_time' claims respectively.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.3.4: OAuth Resource Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.3 - OAuth Resource Server
Requirement ID: V10.3.5
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that the resource server prevents the use of stolen access tokens or replay of access tokens (from unauthorized parties) by requiring sender-constrained access tokens, either Mutual TLS for OAuth 2 or OAuth 2 Demonstration of Proof of Possession (DPoP).
summary: Verify that the resource server prevents the use of stolen access tokens or replay of access tokens (from unauthorized parties) by requiring sender-constrained access tokens, either Mutual TLS for OAuth 2 or OAuth 2 Demonstration of Proof of Possession (DPoP).

content:

Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.15
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that, for a server-side client (which is not executed on the end-user device), the authorization server ensures that the 'authorization_details' parameter value is from the client backend and that the user has not tampered with it. For example, by requiring the usage of pushed authorization request (PAR) or JWT-secured Authorization Request (JAR).
summary: Verify that, for a server-side client (which is not executed on the end-user device), the authorization server ensures that the 'authorization_details' parameter value is from the client backend and that the user has not tampered with it. For example, by requiring the usage of pushed authorization request (PAR) or JWT-secured Authorization Request (JAR).
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.15: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.16
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that the client is confidential and the authorization server requires the use of strong client authentication methods (based on public-key cryptography and resistant to replay attacks), such as mutual TLS ('tls_client_auth', 'self_signed_tls_client_auth') or private key JWT ('private_key_jwt').
summary: Verify that the client is confidential and the authorization server requires the use of strong client authentication methods (based on public-key cryptography and resistant to replay attacks), such as mutual TLS ('tls_client_auth', 'self_signed_tls_client_auth') or private key JWT ('private_key_jwt').
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.16: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.2
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that, if the authorization server returns the authorization code in the authorization response, it can be used only once for a token request. For the second valid request with an authorization code that has already been used to issue an access token, the authorization server must reject a token request and revoke any issued tokens related to the authorization code.
summary: Verify that, if the authorization server returns the authorization code in the authorization response, it can be used only once for a token request. For the second valid request with an authorization code that has already been used to issue an access token, the authorization server must reject a token request and revoke any issued tokens related to the authorization code.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.2: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.3
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that the authorization code is short-lived. The maximum lifetime can be up to 10 minutes for L1 and L2 applications and up to 1 minute for L3 applications.
summary: Verify that the authorization code is short-lived. The maximum lifetime can be up to 10 minutes for L1 and L2 applications and up to 1 minute for L3 applications.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.3: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.4
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that for a given client, the authorization server only allows the usage of grants that this client needs to use. Note that the grants 'token' (Implicit flow) and 'password' (Resource Owner Password Credentials flow) must no longer be used.
summary: Verify that for a given client, the authorization server only allows the usage of grants that this client needs to use. Note that the grants 'token' (Implicit flow) and 'password' (Resource Owner Password Credentials flow) must no longer be used.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.4: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.5
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that the authorization server mitigates refresh token replay attacks for public clients, preferably using sender-constrained refresh tokens, i.e., Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) or Certificate-Bound Access Tokens using mutual TLS (mTLS). For L1 and L2 applications, refresh token rotation may be used. If refresh token rotation is used, the authorization server must invalidate the refresh token after usage, and revoke all refresh tokens for that authorization if an already used and invalidated refresh token is provided.
summary: Verify that the authorization server mitigates refresh token replay attacks for public clients, preferably using sender-constrained refresh tokens, i.e., Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) or Certificate-Bound Access Tokens using mutual TLS (mTLS). For L1 and L2 applications, refresh token rotation may be used. If refresh token rotation is used, the authorization server must invalidate the refresh token after usage, and revoke all refresh tokens for that authorization if an already used and invalidated refresh token is provided.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.5: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.6
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that, if the code grant is used, the authorization server mitigates authorization code interception attacks by requiring proof key for code exchange (PKCE). For authorization requests, the authorization server must require a valid 'code_challenge' value and must not accept a 'code_challenge_method' value of 'plain'. For a token request, it must require validation of the 'code_verifier' parameter.
summary: Verify that, if the code grant is used, the authorization server mitigates authorization code interception attacks by requiring proof key for code exchange (PKCE). For authorization requests, the authorization server must require a valid 'code_challenge' value and must not accept a 'code_challenge_method' value of 'plain'. For a token request, it must require validation of the 'code_verifier' parameter.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.6: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.7
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that if the authorization server supports unauthenticated dynamic client registration, it mitigates the risk of malicious client applications. It must validate client metadata such as any registered URIs, ensure the user's consent, and warn the user before processing an authorization request with an untrusted client application.
summary: Verify that if the authorization server supports unauthenticated dynamic client registration, it mitigates the risk of malicious client applications. It must validate client metadata such as any registered URIs, ensure the user's consent, and warn the user before processing an authorization request with an untrusted client application.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.7: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.8
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that refresh tokens have an absolute expiration, including if sliding refresh token expiration is applied.
summary: Verify that refresh tokens have an absolute expiration, including if sliding refresh token expiration is applied.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.8: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.4 - OAuth Authorization Server
Requirement ID: V10.4.9
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that refresh tokens and reference access tokens can be revoked by an authorized user using the authorization server user interface, to mitigate the risk of malicious clients or stolen tokens.
summary: Verify that refresh tokens and reference access tokens can be revoked by an authorized user using the authorization server user interface, to mitigate the risk of malicious clients or stolen tokens.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.4.9: OAuth Authorization Server

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.5 - OIDC Client
Requirement ID: V10.5.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the client (as the relying party) mitigates ID Token replay attacks. For example, by ensuring that the 'nonce' claim in the ID Token matches the 'nonce' value sent in the authentication request to the OpenID Provider (in OAuth2 refereed to as the authorization request sent to the authorization server).
summary: Verify that the client (as the relying party) mitigates ID Token replay attacks. For example, by ensuring that the 'nonce' claim in the ID Token matches the 'nonce' value sent in the authentication request to the OpenID Provider (in OAuth2 refereed to as the authorization request sent to the authorization server).
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.5.1: OIDC Client

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.5 - OIDC Client
Requirement ID: V10.5.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the client uniquely identifies the user from ID Token claims, usually the 'sub' claim, which cannot be reassigned to other users (for the scope of an identity provider).
summary: Verify that the client uniquely identifies the user from ID Token claims, usually the 'sub' claim, which cannot be reassigned to other users (for the scope of an identity provider).
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.5.2: OIDC Client

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.5 - OIDC Client
Requirement ID: V10.5.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the client rejects attempts by a malicious authorization server to impersonate another authorization server through authorization server metadata. The client must reject authorization server metadata if the issuer URL in the authorization server metadata does not exactly match the pre-configured issuer URL expected by the client.
summary: Verify that the client rejects attempts by a malicious authorization server to impersonate another authorization server through authorization server metadata. The client must reject authorization server metadata if the issuer URL in the authorization server metadata does not exactly match the pre-configured issuer URL expected by the client.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.5.3: OIDC Client

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.5 - OIDC Client
Requirement ID: V10.5.4
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the client validates that the ID Token is intended to be used for that client (audience) by checking that the 'aud' claim from the token is equal to the 'client_id' value for the client.
summary: Verify that the client validates that the ID Token is intended to be used for that client (audience) by checking that the 'aud' claim from the token is equal to the 'client_id' value for the client.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.5.4: OIDC Client

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.5 - OIDC Client
Requirement ID: V10.5.5
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that, when using OIDC back-channel logout, the relying party mitigates denial of service through forced logout and cross-JWT confusion in the logout flow. The client must verify that the logout token is correctly typed with a value of 'logout+jwt', contains the 'event' claim with the correct member name, and does not contain a 'nonce' claim. Note that it is also recommended to have a short expiration (e.g., 2 minutes).
summary: Verify that, when using OIDC back-channel logout, the relying party mitigates denial of service through forced logout and cross-JWT confusion in the logout flow. The client must verify that the logout token is correctly typed with a value of 'logout+jwt', contains the 'event' claim with the correct member name, and does not contain a 'nonce' claim. Note that it is also recommended to have a short expiration (e.g., 2 minutes).
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.5.5: OIDC Client

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.6 - OpenID Provider
Requirement ID: V10.6.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the OpenID Provider only allows values 'code', 'ciba', 'id_token', or 'id_token code' for response mode. Note that 'code' is preferred over 'id_token code' (the OIDC Hybrid flow), and 'token' (any Implicit flow) must not be used.
summary: Verify that the OpenID Provider only allows values 'code', 'ciba', 'id_token', or 'id_token code' for response mode. Note that 'code' is preferred over 'id_token code' (the OIDC Hybrid flow), and 'token' (any Implicit flow) must not be used.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.6.1: OpenID Provider

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.6 - OpenID Provider
Requirement ID: V10.6.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the OpenID Provider mitigates denial of service through forced logout. By obtaining explicit confirmation from the end-user or, if present, validating parameters in the logout request (initiated by the relying party), such as the 'id_token_hint'.
summary: Verify that the OpenID Provider mitigates denial of service through forced logout. By obtaining explicit confirmation from the end-user or, if present, validating parameters in the logout request (initiated by the relying party), such as the 'id_token_hint'.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.6.2: OpenID Provider

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.7 - Consent Management
Requirement ID: V10.7.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the authorization server ensures that the user consents to each authorization request. If the identity of the client cannot be assured, the authorization server must always explicitly prompt the user for consent.
summary: Verify that the authorization server ensures that the user consents to each authorization request. If the identity of the client cannot be assured, the authorization server must always explicitly prompt the user for consent.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.7.1: Consent Management

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.7 - Consent Management
Requirement ID: V10.7.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that when the authorization server prompts for user consent, it presents sufficient and clear information about what is being consented to. When applicable, this should include the nature of the requested authorizations (typically based on scope, resource server, Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) authorization details), the identity of the authorized application, and the lifetime of these authorizations.
summary: Verify that when the authorization server prompts for user consent, it presents sufficient and clear information about what is being consented to. When applicable, this should include the nature of the requested authorizations (typically based on scope, resource server, Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) authorization details), the identity of the authorized application, and the lifetime of these authorizations.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.7.2: Consent Management

content:
Chapter: V10 - OAuth and OIDC
Section: V10.7 - Consent Management
Requirement ID: V10.7.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the user can review, modify, and revoke consents which the user has granted through the authorization server.
summary: Verify that the user can review, modify, and revoke consents which the user has granted through the authorization server.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V10.7.3: Consent Management

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.1 - Cryptographic Inventory and Documentation
Requirement ID: V11.1.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that there is a documented policy for management of cryptographic keys and a cryptographic key lifecycle that follows a key management standard such as NIST SP 800-57. This should include ensuring that keys are not overshared (for example, with more than two entities for shared secrets and more than one entity for private keys).
summary: Verify that there is a documented policy for management of cryptographic keys and a cryptographic key lifecycle that follows a key management standard such as NIST SP 800-57. This should include ensuring that keys are not overshared (for example, with more than two entities for shared secrets and more than one entity for private keys).
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.1.1: Cryptographic Inventory and Documentation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.1 - Cryptographic Inventory and Documentation
Requirement ID: V11.1.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that a cryptographic inventory is performed, maintained, regularly updated, and includes all cryptographic keys, algorithms, and certificates used by the application. It must also document where keys can and cannot be used in the system, and the types of data that can and cannot be protected using the keys.
summary: Verify that a cryptographic inventory is performed, maintained, regularly updated, and includes all cryptographic keys, algorithms, and certificates used by the application. It must also document where keys can and cannot be used in the system, and the types of data that can and cannot be protected using the keys.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.1.2: Cryptographic Inventory and Documentation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.1 - Cryptographic Inventory and Documentation
Requirement ID: V11.1.3
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that cryptographic discovery mechanisms are employed to identify all instances of cryptography in the system, including encryption, hashing, and signing operations.
summary: Verify that cryptographic discovery mechanisms are employed to identify all instances of cryptography in the system, including encryption, hashing, and signing operations.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.1.3: Cryptographic Inventory and Documentation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.1 - Cryptographic Inventory and Documentation
Requirement ID: V11.1.4
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that a cryptographic inventory is maintained. This must include a documented plan that outlines the migration path to new cryptographic standards, such as post-quantum cryptography, in order to react to future threats.
summary: Verify that a cryptographic inventory is maintained. This must include a documented plan that outlines the migration path to new cryptographic standards, such as post-quantum cryptography, in order to react to future threats.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.1.4: Cryptographic Inventory and Documentation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.2 - Secure Cryptography Implementation
Requirement ID: V11.2.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that industry-validated implementations (including libraries and hardware-accelerated implementations) are used for cryptographic operations.
summary: Verify that industry-validated implementations (including libraries and hardware-accelerated implementations) are used for cryptographic operations.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.2.1: Secure Cryptography Implementation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.2 - Secure Cryptography Implementation
Requirement ID: V11.2.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the application is designed with crypto agility such that random number, authenticated encryption, MAC, or hashing algorithms, key lengths, rounds, ciphers and modes can be reconfigured, upgraded, or swapped at any time, to protect against cryptographic breaks. Similarly, it must also be possible to replace keys and passwords and re-encrypt data. This will allow for seamless upgrades to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), once high-assurance implementations of approved PQC schemes or standards are widely available.
summary: Verify that the application is designed with crypto agility such that random number, authenticated encryption, MAC, or hashing algorithms, key lengths, rounds, ciphers and modes can be reconfigured, upgraded, or swapped at any time, to protect against cryptographic breaks. Similarly, it must also be possible to replace keys and passwords and re-encrypt data. This will allow for seamless upgrades to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), once high-assurance implementations of approved PQC schemes or standards are widely available.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.2.2: Secure Cryptography Implementation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.2 - Secure Cryptography Implementation
Requirement ID: V11.2.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that all cryptographic primitives utilize a minimum of 128-bits of security based on the algorithm, key size, and configuration. For example, a 256-bit ECC key provides roughly 128 bits of security where RSA requires a 3072-bit key to achieve 128 bits of security.
summary: Verify that all cryptographic primitives utilize a minimum of 128-bits of security based on the algorithm, key size, and configuration. For example, a 256-bit ECC key provides roughly 128 bits of security where RSA requires a 3072-bit key to achieve 128 bits of security.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.2.3: Secure Cryptography Implementation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.2 - Secure Cryptography Implementation
Requirement ID: V11.2.4
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that all cryptographic operations are constant-time, with no 'short-circuit' operations in comparisons, calculations, or returns, to avoid leaking information.
summary: Verify that all cryptographic operations are constant-time, with no 'short-circuit' operations in comparisons, calculations, or returns, to avoid leaking information.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.2.4: Secure Cryptography Implementation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.2 - Secure Cryptography Implementation
Requirement ID: V11.2.5
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that all cryptographic modules fail securely, and errors are handled in a way that does not enable vulnerabilities, such as Padding Oracle attacks.
summary: Verify that all cryptographic modules fail securely, and errors are handled in a way that does not enable vulnerabilities, such as Padding Oracle attacks.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.2.5: Secure Cryptography Implementation

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.3 - Encryption Algorithms
Requirement ID: V11.3.1
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that insecure block modes (e.g., ECB) and weak padding schemes (e.g., PKCS#1 v1.5) are not used.
summary: Verify that insecure block modes (e.g., ECB) and weak padding schemes (e.g., PKCS#1 v1.5) are not used.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.3.1: Encryption Algorithms

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.3 - Encryption Algorithms
Requirement ID: V11.3.2
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that only approved ciphers and modes such as AES with GCM are used.
summary: Verify that only approved ciphers and modes such as AES with GCM are used.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.3.2: Encryption Algorithms

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.3 - Encryption Algorithms
Requirement ID: V11.3.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that encrypted data is protected against unauthorized modification preferably by using an approved authenticated encryption method or by combining an approved encryption method with an approved MAC algorithm.
summary: Verify that encrypted data is protected against unauthorized modification preferably by using an approved authenticated encryption method or by combining an approved encryption method with an approved MAC algorithm.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.3.3: Encryption Algorithms

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.3 - Encryption Algorithms
Requirement ID: V11.3.4
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that nonces, initialization vectors, and other single-use numbers are not used for more than one encryption key and data-element pair. The method of generation must be appropriate for the algorithm being used.
summary: Verify that nonces, initialization vectors, and other single-use numbers are not used for more than one encryption key and data-element pair. The method of generation must be appropriate for the algorithm being used.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.3.4: Encryption Algorithms

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.3 - Encryption Algorithms
Requirement ID: V11.3.5
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that any combination of an encryption algorithm and a MAC algorithm is operating in encrypt-then-MAC mode.
summary: Verify that any combination of an encryption algorithm and a MAC algorithm is operating in encrypt-then-MAC mode.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.3.5: Encryption Algorithms

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.4 - Hashing and Hash-based Functions
Requirement ID: V11.4.1
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that only approved hash functions are used for general cryptographic use cases, including digital signatures, HMAC, KDF, and random bit generation. Disallowed hash functions, such as MD5, must not be used for any cryptographic purpose.
summary: Verify that only approved hash functions are used for general cryptographic use cases, including digital signatures, HMAC, KDF, and random bit generation. Disallowed hash functions, such as MD5, must not be used for any cryptographic purpose.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.4.1: Hashing and Hash-based Functions

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.4 - Hashing and Hash-based Functions
Requirement ID: V11.4.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that passwords are stored using an approved, computationally intensive, key derivation function (also known as a "password hashing function"), with parameter settings configured based on current guidance. The settings should balance security and performance to make brute-force attacks sufficiently challenging for the required level of security.
summary: Verify that passwords are stored using an approved, computationally intensive, key derivation function (also known as a "password hashing function"), with parameter settings configured based on current guidance. The settings should balance security and performance to make brute-force attacks sufficiently challenging for the required level of security.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.4.2: Hashing and Hash-based Functions

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.4 - Hashing and Hash-based Functions
Requirement ID: V11.4.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that hash functions used in digital signatures, as part of data authentication or data integrity are collision resistant and have appropriate bit-lengths. If collision resistance is required, the output length must be at least 256 bits. If only resistance to second pre-image attacks is required, the output length must be at least 128 bits.
summary: Verify that hash functions used in digital signatures, as part of data authentication or data integrity are collision resistant and have appropriate bit-lengths. If collision resistance is required, the output length must be at least 256 bits. If only resistance to second pre-image attacks is required, the output length must be at least 128 bits.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.4.3: Hashing and Hash-based Functions

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.4 - Hashing and Hash-based Functions
Requirement ID: V11.4.4
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the application uses approved key derivation functions with key stretching parameters when deriving secret keys from passwords. The parameters in use must balance security and performance to prevent brute-force attacks from compromising the resulting cryptographic key.
summary: Verify that the application uses approved key derivation functions with key stretching parameters when deriving secret keys from passwords. The parameters in use must balance security and performance to prevent brute-force attacks from compromising the resulting cryptographic key.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.4.4: Hashing and Hash-based Functions

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.5 - Random Values
Requirement ID: V11.5.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that all random numbers and strings which are intended to be non-guessable must be generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and have at least 128 bits of entropy. Note that UUIDs do not respect this condition.
summary: Verify that all random numbers and strings which are intended to be non-guessable must be generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and have at least 128 bits of entropy. Note that UUIDs do not respect this condition.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.5.1: Random Values

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.5 - Random Values
Requirement ID: V11.5.2
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that the random number generation mechanism in use is designed to work securely, even under heavy demand.
summary: Verify that the random number generation mechanism in use is designed to work securely, even under heavy demand.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.5.2: Random Values

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.6 - Public Key Cryptography
Requirement ID: V11.6.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that only approved cryptographic algorithms and modes of operation are used for key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification. Key generation algorithms must not generate insecure keys vulnerable to known attacks, for example, RSA keys which are vulnerable to Fermat factorization.
summary: Verify that only approved cryptographic algorithms and modes of operation are used for key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification. Key generation algorithms must not generate insecure keys vulnerable to known attacks, for example, RSA keys which are vulnerable to Fermat factorization.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.6.1: Public Key Cryptography

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.6 - Public Key Cryptography
Requirement ID: V11.6.2
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that approved cryptographic algorithms are used for key exchange (such as Diffie-Hellman) with a focus on ensuring that key exchange mechanisms use secure parameters. This will prevent attacks on the key establishment process which could lead to adversary-in-the-middle attacks or cryptographic breaks.
summary: Verify that approved cryptographic algorithms are used for key exchange (such as Diffie-Hellman) with a focus on ensuring that key exchange mechanisms use secure parameters. This will prevent attacks on the key establishment process which could lead to adversary-in-the-middle attacks or cryptographic breaks.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.6.2: Public Key Cryptography

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.7 - In-Use Data Cryptography
Requirement ID: V11.7.1
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that full memory encryption is in use that protects sensitive data while it is in use, preventing access by unauthorized users or processes.
summary: Verify that full memory encryption is in use that protects sensitive data while it is in use, preventing access by unauthorized users or processes.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V11.7.1: In-Use Data Cryptography

content:
Chapter: V11 - Cryptography
Section: V11.7 - In-Use Data Cryptography
Requirement ID: V11.7.2
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that data minimization ensures the minimal amount of data is exposed during processing, and ensure that data is encrypted immediately after use or as soon as feasible.

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.1 - General TLS Security Guidance
Requirement ID: V12.1.1
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The latest version of the TLS protocol must be the preferred option.
summary: Verify that only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The latest version of the TLS protocol must be the preferred option.

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.1 - General TLS Security Guidance
Requirement ID: V12.1.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that only recommended cipher suites are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy.
summary: Verify that only recommended cipher suites are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.1.2: General TLS Security Guidance

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.1 - General TLS Security Guidance
Requirement ID: V12.1.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the application validates that mTLS client certificates are trusted before using the certificate identity for authentication or authorization.
summary: Verify that the application validates that mTLS client certificates are trusted before using the certificate identity for authentication or authorization.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.1.3: General TLS Security Guidance

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.1 - General TLS Security Guidance
Requirement ID: V12.1.4
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that proper certification revocation, such as Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling, is enabled and configured.
summary: Verify that proper certification revocation, such as Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling, is enabled and configured.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.1.4: General TLS Security Guidance

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.1 - General TLS Security Guidance
Requirement ID: V12.1.5
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) is enabled in the application's TLS settings to prevent exposure of sensitive metadata, such as the Server Name Indication (SNI), during TLS handshake processes.
summary: Verify that Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) is enabled in the application's TLS settings to prevent exposure of sensitive metadata, such as the Server Name Indication (SNI), during TLS handshake processes.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.1.5: General TLS Security Guidance

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.2 - HTTPS Communication with External Facing Services
Requirement ID: V12.2.1
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that TLS is used for all connectivity between a client and external facing, HTTP-based services, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.
summary: Verify that TLS is used for all connectivity between a client and external facing, HTTP-based services, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.2 - HTTPS Communication with External Facing Services
Requirement ID: V12.2.2
Verification Level: L1

summary: Verify that external facing services use publicly trusted TLS certificates.

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.3 - General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement ID: V12.3.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols.
summary: Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.3.1: General Service to Service Communication Security

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.3 - General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement ID: V12.3.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that TLS clients validate certificates received before communicating with a TLS server.
summary: Verify that TLS clients validate certificates received before communicating with a TLS server.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.3.2: General Service to Service Communication Security

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.3 - General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement ID: V12.3.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that TLS or another appropriate transport encryption mechanism used for all connectivity between internal, HTTP-based services within the application, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.
summary: Verify that TLS or another appropriate transport encryption mechanism used for all connectivity between internal, HTTP-based services within the application, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.3.3: General Service to Service Communication Security

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.3 - General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement ID: V12.3.4
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates.
summary: Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.3.4: General Service to Service Communication Security

content:
Chapter: V12 - Secure Communication
Section: V12.3 - General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement ID: V12.3.5
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that services communicating internally within a system (intra-service communications) use strong authentication to ensure that each endpoint is verified. Strong authentication methods, such as TLS client authentication, must be employed to ensure identity, using public-key infrastructure and mechanisms that are resistant to replay attacks. For microservice architectures, consider using a service mesh to simplify certificate management and enhance security.
summary: Verify that services communicating internally within a system (intra-service communications) use strong authentication to ensure that each endpoint is verified. Strong authentication methods, such as TLS client authentication, must be employed to ensure identity, using public-key infrastructure and mechanisms that are resistant to replay attacks. For microservice architectures, consider using a service mesh to simplify certificate management and enhance security.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V12.3.5: General Service to Service Communication Security

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.1 - Configuration Documentation
Requirement ID: V13.1.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that all communication needs for the application are documented. This must include external services which the application relies upon and cases where an end user might be able to provide an external location to which the application will then connect.
summary: Verify that all communication needs for the application are documented. This must include external services which the application relies upon and cases where an end user might be able to provide an external location to which the application will then connect.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.1.1: Configuration Documentation

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.1 - Configuration Documentation
Requirement ID: V13.1.2
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that for each service the application uses, the documentation defines the maximum number of concurrent connections (e.g., connection pool limits) and how the application behaves when that limit is reached, including any fallback or recovery mechanisms, to prevent denial of service conditions.
summary: Verify that for each service the application uses, the documentation defines the maximum number of concurrent connections (e.g., connection pool limits) and how the application behaves when that limit is reached, including any fallback or recovery mechanisms, to prevent denial of service conditions.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.1.2: Configuration Documentation

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.1 - Configuration Documentation
Requirement ID: V13.1.3
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that the application documentation defines resource‑management strategies for every external system or service it uses (e.g., databases, file handles, threads, HTTP connections). This should include resource‑release procedures, timeout settings, failure handling, and where retry logic is implemented, specifying retry limits, delays, and back‑off algorithms. For synchronous HTTP request–response operations it should mandate short timeouts and either disable retries or strictly limit retries to prevent cascading delays and resource exhaustion.
summary: Verify that the application documentation defines resource‑management strategies for every external system or service it uses (e.g., databases, file handles, threads, HTTP connections). This should include resource‑release procedures, timeout settings, failure handling, and where retry logic is implemented, specifying retry limits, delays, and back‑off algorithms. For synchronous HTTP request–response operations it should mandate short timeouts and either disable retries or strictly limit retries to prevent cascading delays and resource exhaustion.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.1.3: Configuration Documentation

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.1 - Configuration Documentation
Requirement ID: V13.1.4
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that the application's documentation defines the secrets that are critical for the security of the application and a schedule for rotating them, based on the organization's threat model and business requirements.
summary: Verify that the application's documentation defines the secrets that are critical for the security of the application and a schedule for rotating them, based on the organization's threat model and business requirements.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.1.4: Configuration Documentation

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.2 - Backend Communication Configuration
Requirement ID: V13.2.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that communications between backend application components that don't support the application's standard user session mechanism, including APIs, middleware, and data layers, are authenticated. Authentication must use individual service accounts, short-term tokens, or certificate-based authentication and not unchanging credentials such as passwords, API keys, or shared accounts with privileged access.
summary: Verify that communications between backend application components that don't support the application's standard user session mechanism, including APIs, middleware, and data layers, are authenticated. Authentication must use individual service accounts, short-term tokens, or certificate-based authentication and not unchanging credentials such as passwords, API keys, or shared accounts with privileged access.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.2.1: Backend Communication Configuration

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.2 - Backend Communication Configuration
Requirement ID: V13.2.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that communications between backend application components, including local or operating system services, APIs, middleware, and data layers, are performed with accounts assigned the least necessary privileges.
summary: Verify that communications between backend application components, including local or operating system services, APIs, middleware, and data layers, are performed with accounts assigned the least necessary privileges.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.2.2: Backend Communication Configuration

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.2 - Backend Communication Configuration
Requirement ID: V13.2.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that if a credential has to be used for service authentication, the credential being used by the consumer is not a default credential (e.g., root/root or admin/admin).
summary: Verify that if a credential has to be used for service authentication, the credential being used by the consumer is not a default credential (e.g., root/root or admin/admin).
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.2.3: Backend Communication Configuration

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.2 - Backend Communication Configuration
Requirement ID: V13.2.4
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that an allowlist is used to define the external resources or systems with which the application is permitted to communicate (e.g., for outbound requests, data loads, or file access). This allowlist can be implemented at the application layer, web server, firewall, or a combination of different layers.
summary: Verify that an allowlist is used to define the external resources or systems with which the application is permitted to communicate (e.g., for outbound requests, data loads, or file access). This allowlist can be implemented at the application layer, web server, firewall, or a combination of different layers.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.2.4: Backend Communication Configuration

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.2 - Backend Communication Configuration
Requirement ID: V13.2.5
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allowlist of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data or files from.
summary: Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allowlist of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data or files from.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.2.5: Backend Communication Configuration

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.2 - Backend Communication Configuration
Requirement ID: V13.2.6
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that where the application connects to separate services, it follows the documented configuration for each connection, such as maximum parallel connections, behavior when maximum allowed connections is reached, connection timeouts, and retry strategies.
summary: Verify that where the application connects to separate services, it follows the documented configuration for each connection, such as maximum parallel connections, behavior when maximum allowed connections is reached, connection timeouts, and retry strategies.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.2.6: Backend Communication Configuration

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.3 - Secret Management
Requirement ID: V13.3.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that a secrets management solution, such as a key vault, is used to securely create, store, control access to, and destroy backend secrets. These could include passwords, key material, integrations with databases and third-party systems, keys and seeds for time-based tokens, other internal secrets, and API keys. Secrets must not be included in application source code or included in build artifacts. For an L3 application, this must involve a hardware-backed solution such as an HSM.
summary: Verify that a secrets management solution, such as a key vault, is used to securely create, store, control access to, and destroy backend secrets. These could include passwords, key material, integrations with databases and third-party systems, keys and seeds for time-based tokens, other internal secrets, and API keys. Secrets must not be included in application source code or included in build artifacts. For an L3 application, this must involve a hardware-backed solution such as an HSM.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V13.3.1: Secret Management

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.3 - Secret Management
Requirement ID: V13.3.2
Verification Level: L2

Verify that access to secret assets adheres to the principle of least privilege.
summary: Verify that access to secret assets adheres to the principle of least privilege.

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.3 - Secret Management
Requirement ID: V13.3.3
Verification Level: L3

Verify that all cryptographic operations are performed using an isolated security module (such as a vault or hardware security module) to securely manage and protect key material from exposure outside of the security module.
summary: Verify that all cryptographic operations are performed using an isolated security module (such as a vault or hardware security module) to securely manage and protect key material from exposure outside of the security module.

content:
Chapter: V13 - Configuration
Section: V13.3 - Secret Management
Requirement ID: V13.3.4
Verification Level: L3

summary: Verify that secrets are configured to expire and be rotated based on the application's documentation.

Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that the application is deployed either without any source control metadata, including the .git or .svn folders, or in a way that these folders are inaccessible both externally and to the application itself.

Verification Level: L2

Verification Level: L2

Verification Level: L2

Verification Level: L2

Section: V13.4 - Unintended Information Leakage

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.1 - Data Protection Documentation
Requirement ID: V14.1.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels. This includes data that is only encoded and therefore easily decoded, such as Base64 strings or the plaintext payload inside a JWT. Protection levels need to take into account any data protection and privacy regulations and standards which the application is required to comply with.
summary: Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels. This includes data that is only encoded and therefore easily decoded, such as Base64 strings or the plaintext payload inside a JWT. Protection levels need to take into account any data protection and privacy regulations and standards which the application is required to comply with.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.1.1: Data Protection Documentation

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.1 - Data Protection Documentation
Requirement ID: V14.1.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that all sensitive data protection levels have a documented set of protection requirements. This must include (but not be limited to) requirements related to general encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, database-level encryption, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies to be used, and other confidentiality requirements.
summary: Verify that all sensitive data protection levels have a documented set of protection requirements. This must include (but not be limited to) requirements related to general encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, database-level encryption, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies to be used, and other confidentiality requirements.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.1.2: Data Protection Documentation

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.2 - General Data Protection
Requirement ID: V14.2.1
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token.
summary: Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.2.1: General Data Protection

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.2 - General Data Protection
Requirement ID: V14.2.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches, or ensures that the data is securely purged after use.
summary: Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches, or ensures that the data is securely purged after use.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.2.2: General Data Protection

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.2 - General Data Protection
Requirement ID: V14.2.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that defined sensitive data is not sent to untrusted parties (e.g., user trackers) to prevent unwanted collection of data outside of the application's control.
summary: Verify that defined sensitive data is not sent to untrusted parties (e.g., user trackers) to prevent unwanted collection of data outside of the application's control.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.2.3: General Data Protection

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.2 - General Data Protection
Requirement ID: V14.2.4
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies, are implemented as defined in the documentation for the specific data's protection level.
summary: Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies, are implemented as defined in the documentation for the specific data's protection level.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.2.4: General Data Protection

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.2 - General Data Protection
Requirement ID: V14.2.5
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that caching mechanisms are configured to only cache responses which have the expected content type for that resource and do not contain sensitive, dynamic content. The web server should return a 404 or 302 response when a non-existent file is accessed rather than returning a different, valid file. This should prevent Web Cache Deception attacks.
summary: Verify that caching mechanisms are configured to only cache responses which have the expected content type for that resource and do not contain sensitive, dynamic content. The web server should return a 404 or 302 response when a non-existent file is accessed rather than returning a different, valid file. This should prevent Web Cache Deception attacks.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.2.5: General Data Protection

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.2 - General Data Protection
Requirement ID: V14.2.6
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that the application only returns the minimum required sensitive data for the application's functionality. For example, only returning some of the digits of a credit card number and not the full number. If the complete data is required, it should be masked in the user interface unless the user specifically views it.
summary: Verify that the application only returns the minimum required sensitive data for the application's functionality. For example, only returning some of the digits of a credit card number and not the full number. If the complete data is required, it should be masked in the user interface unless the user specifically views it.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.2.6: General Data Protection

content:
Chapter: V14 - Data Protection
Section: V14.2 - General Data Protection
Requirement ID: V14.2.7
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that sensitive information is subject to data retention classification, ensuring that outdated or unnecessary data is deleted automatically, on a defined schedule, or as the situation requires.
summary: Verify that sensitive information is subject to data retention classification, ensuring that outdated or unnecessary data is deleted automatically, on a defined schedule, or as the situation requires.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V14.2.7: General Data Protection

content:

Section: V14.2 - General Data Protection
Requirement ID: V14.2.8
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that sensitive information is removed from the metadata of user-submitted files unless storage is consented to by the user.
summary: Verify that sensitive information is removed from the metadata of user-submitted files unless storage is consented to by the user.

content:

Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage, such as the browser DOM, after the client or session is terminated. The 'Clear-Site-Data' HTTP response header field may be able to help with this but the client-side should also be able to clear up if the server connection is not available when the session is terminated.

content:

Requirement ID: V14.3.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:

summary: Verify that the application sets sufficient anti-caching HTTP response header fields (i.e., Cache-Control: no-store) so that sensitive data is not cached in browsers.

content:

Verification Level: L2

summary: Verify that data stored in browser storage (such as localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, or cookies) does not contain sensitive data, with the exception of session tokens.

Verify that the application's documentation defines input validation rules for how to check the validity of data items against an expected structure. This could be common data formats such as credit card numbers, email addresses, telephone numbers, or it could be an internal data format.
summary: Verify that the application's documentation defines input validation rules for how to check the validity of data items against an expected structure. This could be common data formats such as credit card numbers, email addresses, telephone numbers, or it could be an internal data format.

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.1 - Validation and Business Logic Documentation
Requirement ID: V2.1.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the application's documentation defines how to validate the logical and contextual consistency of combined data items, such as checking that suburb and ZIP code match.
summary: Verify that the application's documentation defines how to validate the logical and contextual consistency of combined data items, such as checking that suburb and ZIP code match.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.1.2: Validation and Business Logic Documentation

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.1 - Validation and Business Logic Documentation
Requirement ID: V2.1.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that expectations for business logic limits and validations are documented, including both per-user and globally across the application.
summary: Verify that expectations for business logic limits and validations are documented, including both per-user and globally across the application.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.1.3: Validation and Business Logic Documentation

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.2 - Input Validation
Requirement ID: V2.2.1
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. This should either use positive validation against an allow list of values, patterns, and ranges, or be based on comparing the input to an expected structure and logical limits according to predefined rules. For L1, this can focus on input which is used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this should apply to all input.
summary: Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. This should either use positive validation against an allow list of values, patterns, and ranges, or be based on comparing the input to an expected structure and logical limits according to predefined rules. For L1, this can focus on input which is used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this should apply to all input.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.2.1: Input Validation

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.2 - Input Validation
Requirement ID: V2.2.2
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that the application is designed to enforce input validation at a trusted service layer. While client-side validation improves usability and should be encouraged, it must not be relied upon as a security control.
summary: Verify that the application is designed to enforce input validation at a trusted service layer. While client-side validation improves usability and should be encouraged, it must not be relied upon as a security control.

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.2 - Input Validation
Requirement ID: V2.2.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that the application ensures that combinations of related data items are reasonable according to the pre-defined rules.
summary: Verify that the application ensures that combinations of related data items are reasonable according to the pre-defined rules.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.2.3: Input Validation

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.3 - Business Logic Security
Requirement ID: V2.3.1
Verification Level: L1

Requirement:
Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in the expected sequential step order and without skipping steps.
summary: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in the expected sequential step order and without skipping steps.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.3.1: Business Logic Security

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.3 - Business Logic Security
Requirement ID: V2.3.2
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that business logic limits are implemented per the application's documentation to avoid business logic flaws being exploited.
summary: Verify that business logic limits are implemented per the application's documentation to avoid business logic flaws being exploited.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.3.2: Business Logic Security

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.3 - Business Logic Security
Requirement ID: V2.3.3
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that transactions are being used at the business logic level such that either a business logic operation succeeds in its entirety or it is rolled back to the previous correct state.
summary: Verify that transactions are being used at the business logic level such that either a business logic operation succeeds in its entirety or it is rolled back to the previous correct state.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.3.3: Business Logic Security

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.3 - Business Logic Security
Requirement ID: V2.3.4
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that business logic level locking mechanisms are used to ensure that limited quantity resources (such as theater seats or delivery slots) cannot be double-booked by manipulating the application's logic.
summary: Verify that business logic level locking mechanisms are used to ensure that limited quantity resources (such as theater seats or delivery slots) cannot be double-booked by manipulating the application's logic.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.3.4: Business Logic Security

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.3 - Business Logic Security
Requirement ID: V2.3.5
Verification Level: L3

Requirement:
Verify that high-value business logic flows require multi-user approval to prevent unauthorized or accidental actions. This could include but is not limited to large monetary transfers, contract approvals, access to classified information, or safety overrides in manufacturing.
summary: Verify that high-value business logic flows require multi-user approval to prevent unauthorized or accidental actions. This could include but is not limited to large monetary transfers, contract approvals, access to classified information, or safety overrides in manufacturing.
title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 V2.3.5: Business Logic Security

content:
Chapter: V2 - Validation and Business Logic
Section: V2.4 - Anti-automation
Requirement ID: V2.4.1
Verification Level: L2

Requirement:
Verify that anti-automation controls are in place to protect against excessive calls to application functions that could lead to data exfiltration, garbage-data creation, quota exhaustion, rate-limit breaches, denial-of-service, or overuse of costly resources.
summary: Verify that anti-automation controls are in place to protect against excessive calls to application functions that could lead to data exfiltration, garbage-data creation, quota exhaustion, rate-limit breaches, denial-of-service, or overuse of costly resources.
